query.description: Keyword search over every tool's name and description (e.g. 'retirement simulation', 'rebalance plan'). Returns the top matching tools and loads them for this session.

names.description: Exact tool names to load, when you already know what you want (e.g. ['get_returns', 'get_rebalance_plan']). Cheaper and more certain than a keyword search. Use INSTEAD of query, not with it.

max_results.description: Maximum tools to return (default 10). Applies to query search only.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring over account NAME or PLATFORM (e.g. 'meridian', 'ibkr'). The cheapest way to find one account.

ids.description: Specific accounts by id OR by exact name (case-insensitive). Names that match nothing, or that are ambiguous, are reported back rather than guessed.

type.description: Exact account type, one of the seven: cash | fixed_deposit | investment | retirement | receivable | credit | loan.

include_archived.description: Set true to include archived (closed) accounts. Default false.

name.description: Account name. Securities account: custodian name ('IBKR'). Currency wallet: 'IBKR USD'.

type.description: cash: bank/e-wallet/physical, spendable, in budget · fixed_deposit: time-locked cash · investment: brokerage/exchange (holdings + settlement cash; a broker's currency wallet is ALSO investment, same institution) · retirement: CPF/SRS/pension · receivable: owed to you · credit: card/BNPL/line of credit, paid from cash · loan: mortgage/auto/personal/student/margin loan

institution.description: Institution / custodian grouping key (e.g. 'IBKR', 'Meridian Bank'). Same value on the securities account and all its currency wallets.

currency.description: 3-letter ISO code. Use the account's native currency (default to the user's base_currency if not specified).

initial_balance.description: Required current balance today, in the account's currency; use 0 when empty. Signed as written — pass a NEGATIVE number for money owed (a card carrying 5000 of debt is -5000); the sign is not flipped for you. Stored as a dated Starting Balance transaction, not a field on the account.

initial_balance_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD tracking-start date — it becomes the Starting Balance transaction's date, and legs before it are ignored. Defaults to today when an opening balance is given.

credit_limit.description: Credit limit in the card's currency (optional)

note.description: Free-form note stored on the account record — display/metadata only. Never read by balances, net worth, dedup, or rules. Defaults to empty.

ref.description: The provider's own id for this account.

name.description: Provider-side account name/label.

mask.description: Last digits the provider shows for this account. Fills `last_four` on the account if it's currently blank.

institution.description: Provider institution display name. Fills `institution` on the account if it's currently blank. Never itself stored on the link.

external_ids.description: Provider-account links to attach at creation — rare; usually set later via update_accounts. Each (source, ref) pair may be linked to only one account; linking one already held elsewhere raises, naming the holder.

apr.description: Interest rate % — credit and loan accounts.

updates.description: The edits to apply. One item is the common case.

account_id.description: Account ID or name from list_accounts.

name.description: New display name. Load-bearing, not cosmetic: account refs resolve by name as well as id, so renaming changes what later calls resolve, and a name that duplicates another live account makes BOTH ambiguous — a ref naming them then fails rather than guessing. Omit to leave unchanged.

institution.description: Custodian grouping key (e.g. 'IBKR'). Same across the securities account and its currency wallets. '' to ungroup.

initial_balance_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD tracking start — the Starting Balance transaction's date. Legs before it are ignored.

credit_limit.description: The card's credit line, a positive number in the account's own currency. Reference metadata shown in the account editor — nothing computes utilization off it and it neither caps spending nor affects balances or net worth.

last_four.description: Last 4 digits of the card/account number. Load-bearing for statement import: an uploaded statement's detected last-4 is matched against this to pick the destination account, so a wrong value silently routes rows to the wrong place.

note.description: Free-text memo about the account itself (e.g. 'joint with Alex, rent and bills'), shown in the account editor. REPLACES the existing note wholesale rather than appending; '' clears it. Unrelated to transaction memos.

archived.description: Set true to archive (hide) or false to restore.

ref.description: The provider's own id for this account.

name.description: Provider-side account name/label.

mask.description: Last digits the provider shows for this account. Fills `last_four` on the account if it's currently blank.

institution.description: Provider institution display name. Fills `institution` on the account if it's currently blank. Never itself stored on the link.

external_ids.description: REPLACES the account's whole list of provider links — omit to leave unchanged, pass [] to unlink everything, or the full desired list otherwise. Each (source, ref) pair may be linked to only one account; linking one already held elsewhere raises, naming the holder.

apr.description: Interest rate % — credit and loan accounts.

statement_close_day.description: Credit: statement close day of month (1–31).

payment_due_day.description: Credit: payment due day of month (1–31).

text.description: The user's free-text description of the account.

account_ids.description: Account IDs or names from list_accounts. Pass one to delete a single account, or several to delete many at once. Each account is deleted independently — one still referenced by live transactions is refused on its own (reported in `refused` with why) without blocking the rest of the batch.

as_of.description: A PAST date (YYYY-MM-DD) for net worth as it stood at that day's end — e.g. the last day of a reported week or month. Omit for today.

account_id.description: Account ID or name from list_accounts.

real_balance.description: The true current balance in the account's native currency (negative for a card you owe on).

against.description: Overrides the call's own `against` for this account only.

date.description: Overrides the call's own `date` for this account only.

accounts.description: BATCH form: reconcile several accounts in ONE call, each to its own real_balance — e.g. checking to 500, savings to 1200, card to -300. When set, the top-level account_id/real_balance are ignored; against/date still apply as the shared default for any item that doesn't set its own.

dry_run.description: If true, compute and return the delta(s) without writing anything. Always use this first to show the user what will change before applying.

txn_ids.description: Transaction ids (from get_transactions) to mark cleared/uncleared, all with the SAME flag — e.g. clearing every matched row after a statement reconciliation. Pass one id to set a single transaction. Each is set independently; one refusal (an account's Starting Balance row can't be uncleared) never blocks the rest.

cleared.description: True to mark cleared, False to mark uncleared.

country.description: 2-letter ISO country code (e.g. US, GB, DE, FR). Required to list specific banks for the EU providers.

query.description: Optional bank-name search filter (e.g. 'Meridian Bank', 'Beacon Bank').

tickers.description: Filter to one symbol, e.g. 'AAPL', or a LIST to match any of several.

limit.description: Max rows to return (default 50). Page further with offset.

offset.description: Rows to skip before applying limit. Default 0.

alerts.description: Create MULTIPLE alerts in one call: [{ticker, op, value, kind?, note?, label?, name?, channels?, asset_class?}, ...]. Omit when creating a single alert via the top-level fields above.

op.description: Comparison direction: the alert fires when live price `op` `value` ('>=' 200 fires at or above 200; '<=' 90 is a stop). Rising-edge — it fires ONCE on the crossing, re-arms when the condition goes false again, and is not deleted by firing.

value.description: Price level in the asset's currency; a percent (0-100] if kind='move'

kind.description: 'price' (default) or 'move': value is a % move vs. previous close ('drops 5% today' = '<=' 5); '>=' fires on a rise of value%, '<=' on a fall.

note.description: Instructions for Lucius when it fires.

name.description: Short display name for the alert, e.g. 'Stop-loss zone'. Optional.

channels.description: Where this alert is ALSO sent when it fires, besides the in-app feed: channel ids ('telegram', 'email', 'webhook'; get_alert_channels lists what's set up). [] = in-app only. Omit on create to use the user's price-alert default.

asset_class.description: Classifies the alert for display/grouping in the Intel UI: equity | crypto | commodity | property | other. Defaults to 'equity'. Does NOT affect when the alert fires (that is op/value alone) and is unrelated to crash-watch thresholds, which are set per class in update_monitoring_config.crash_thresholds.

alert_ids.description: UUID of the alert, or a list to set the SAME change on several at once.

op.description: New comparison direction for the trigger — the alert fires when the live price is `op` `value` (e.g. '>=' 200 fires at or above 200). Omit to leave the existing direction unchanged.

value.description: New trigger price level, in the asset's own quote currency (not the portfolio base); a percent for a 'move' alert. Omit to leave it unchanged.

kind.description: 'price' level or 'move' % vs. previous close; send a new value too.

note.description: Replacement instructions for Lucius to act on when the alert fires (e.g. 'take-profit: check if the move has legs before trimming'). Replaces the whole note, never appends. Omit to leave it unchanged.

label.description: Replacement display name for the alert (defaults to the ticker when the alert was created). Omit to leave it unchanged.

name.description: Replacement short display name for the alert, e.g. 'Stop-loss zone'. Omit to leave it unchanged.

channels.description: Where this alert is ALSO sent when it fires, besides the in-app feed: channel ids ('telegram', 'email', 'webhook'; get_alert_channels lists what's set up). [] = in-app only. Omit on create to use the user's price-alert default.

updates.description: Per-alert overrides when different alerts need different changes in one call: [{alert_id, op?, value?, kind?, note?, label?, name?, channels?}, ...]. Takes precedence over the top-level fields above.

title.description: Short human title shown on the artifact card, e.g. 'May 2026 Spending Overview'.

content.description: html/svg: the COMPLETE self-contained document. pdf: an HTML page to lay out on A4 (omit it when converting with source_artifact_id). xlsx/csv: a JSON table spec — {"sheets": [{"name": "Transactions", "title": "optional heading", "columns": [{"header": "Date", "type": "date"}, {"header": "Amount", "type": "money", "currency": "<code from the tools>"}], "rows": [["2026-09-01", 2750.0]], "totals": ["Amount"]}]}. filename.description: Download filename, e.g. may_2026_spending.html. Derived from the title when omitted.

peers_limit.description: Max peer comparables to return (default 8, max 20).

engine_id.description: Engine id from list_budget_engines (e.g. 'zero_based', 'proportional'). Omit for the book's current home engine.

period.description: Budget period as YYYY-MM (e.g. '2026-06'). Omit for the current month.

operation.description: One of that engine's declared operation ids. Call list_budget_engines first — its response's engines[].operations is the authoritative, always-current list (id/label/params) for both engines: zero_based's ~20 envelope/group/category/assignment ops (assign, move_money, set_target, set_targets, envelope_create, group_create, auto_assign, ...), and 50/30/20's configure/set_group_targets/set_group_excluded/set_envelope_excluded/set_cap/set_caps/copy_targets_to_caps/set_income_categories. An unknown operation for the given engine_id errors, naming the real ones.

params.description: The operation's own parameters, per list_budget_engines' engines[].operations[].params — e.g. zero_based assign: {month, envelope_id, amount}. 50/30/20's groups are the book's Zero-Based groups: configure: {group_targets?: {group_id: percent}, excluded_groups?: [group_id]} starts it; set_group_targets: {targets: {group_id: percent or null}}; set_group_excluded: {group_id, excluded: true|false}; set_envelope_excluded: {envelope_id, excluded: true|false} (one envelope out of the split, still in its group); set_cap: {envelope_id, month: 'YYYY-MM', amount} (applies from that month onward, 0 clears, refused before the current month) or set_caps: {month, caps: {envelope_id: amount}} for several at once; copy_targets_to_caps: {month} seeds caps from Zero-Based's own targets; set_income_categories: {category_ids: [...] or null for every income category}. Moving an envelope to another group is Zero-Based's move_envelopes_to_group.

engine_id.description: Engine id from list_budget_engines to make the book's home lens.

name.description: e.g. 'Emergency fund'

linked_account_ids.description: Optional savings accounts whose SUMMED balance IS the progress (ids from list_accounts)

note.description: Free-form note about the goal, stored on the target and shown with it. Display only — never read by progress, pace, or funding math. Defaults to empty.

goal_id.description: The savings goal to edit, by its id (from get_goals).

name.description: New name for the goal, e.g. 'Emergency fund'. Omit to leave it unchanged.

target_amount.description: New goal amount, in the target's own `currency`. Must be > 0. Omit to leave it unchanged.

current_amount.description: New saved-so-far amount, in the target's own `currency`. IGNORED for progress whenever `linked_account_ids` is non-empty — those accounts' summed live balance is authoritative then. Omit to leave it unchanged.

currency.description: New native 3-letter ISO currency for this target's amounts (progress and pace are compared in the portfolio base after conversion). Omit to leave it unchanged.

linked_account_ids.description: Funding accounts whose SUMMED balance IS the progress (replaces the full list)

category.description: Budget category label tied to this goal, e.g. 'travel'. Stored as a plain label only — it does not link the target to an envelope and does not affect progress or funding. Pass an empty string to clear it; omit to leave it unchanged.

priority.description: Funding order — LOWER is funded first (default 1). Sorts the target list and the funding plan. Omit to leave it unchanged.

status.description: Declared lifecycle state. 'cancelled' is terminal and passes through to reads verbatim. NOTE: reads DERIVE the displayed verdict — a target whose progress meets its amount reads 'completed' whether or not you set it here, and an unmet one reads ahead/on_track/behind/past_due from its pace regardless. Omit to leave it unchanged; confirm cancelled/completed with the user first.

note.description: Replacement free-form note on the goal (replaces the whole note, never appends). Display only. Omit to leave it unchanged.

goal_id.description: The savings goal to delete, by its id (from get_goals). Removes the goal outright — it is not archived and linked accounts are untouched.

linked.description: true = linked to an envelope; false = in none.

envelope.description: Only this envelope's categories (id or name).

categories.description: Batch form of the above — each item is {label, kind?, color?}; independent per item, check `results`.

expense_override.description: Monthly expenses to use in the projection (base currency). Omit to use the actual 3-month average.

months.description: How many months to project. Default 12.

payee_id.description: Link to a payee entity (pay_… id from get_payees or create_payee) instead of auto-resolving one from the description. Expense/income only.

allow_duplicate.description: Book every row even where it looks like a duplicate of one already in the ledger. Set this ONLY when the user has confirmed these are genuinely separate charges — it does not make a re-run safe, it books the rows twice. Duplicates are still reported back to you either way.

force_transfer_rate.description: A transfer whose two legs carry the EXACT SAME NUMBER in different currencies is refused when a known exchange rate says they should not match — this is almost always the source amount copied into the destination leg without actually applying the rate (compute to_amount = amount x rate yourself and re-send first). Set this ONLY when the transfer genuinely cleared at that exact number in both currencies (a stale quote, a peg, a fee-inclusive settlement) — it does not change the amounts, it just books the row as stated.

decisions.description: Per-row resolutions when RE-SUBMITTING a batch that aborted with already_recorded, or reported a row previously_deleted (index into THIS SAME transactions list). Omit on a fresh call.

action.description: create = book as new (for a previously_deleted row: re-book it ONLY because the user explicitly asked for it back). link = fold into existing_id instead of duplicating (never changes its date/amount). skip = book nothing.

existing_id.description: Required for action='link' — the existing_id the already_recorded entry proposed for THIS row.

import_description.description: Short human-readable label for this import batch, e.g. 'Checking Jan–Mar' or 'Card Apr'. Used to identify the batch for rollback.

import_session_id.description: Ties all batches of one split statement together. Omit on the first batch — the result returns the id to pass back on every following batch.

statement_ref_id.description: statement_id of the uploaded file (returned by the upload endpoint and by diff_statement), linking this batch to that statement record.

position_id.description: position_id from get_portfolio. Required unless `position_ids` (the batch form) is used instead.

position_ids.description: Batch form: lots for SEVERAL positions in one call — e.g. every AAPL position held across custodians. `limit`/`offset`/`open_only` apply to EACH position individually (not across the combined set); each position gets its OWN `totals` block — a cost basis is never meaningfully summed across different instruments/currencies, so there is no combined grand total. Omit the single `position_id` field when using this.

open_only.description: Only lots with remaining quantity (default false — closed lots are included). A long-held position accumulates many fully-consumed lots; pass true when you only care about what is still sellable.

limit.description: Max lot rows to return (default 50).

offset.description: Zero-based row offset (default 0) — page through with this when a position has more lots than one page holds. Every lot is reachable.

date_from.description: Window mode, with `date_to` and NO position: every lot ACQUIRED in the window across all holdings (ISO YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive) — 'what did I buy this month'.

date_to.description: Window mode: last acquisition date, ISO YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive.

account_id.description: Window mode only: lots at ONE account (id from list_accounts). Omit for every account.

instrument_id.description: Narrow to disposals of ONE instrument (id from get_portfolio or resolve_instruments). Matches a fully-sold holding too, since realized events outlive the position. Omit for every instrument.

account_id.description: Narrow to disposals booked at ONE account (id from list_accounts) — the custodian's securities account, not its cash wallet. Omit for every account.

instrument_id.description: Narrow to fees paid on ONE instrument (id from get_portfolio or resolve_instruments). Omit for every instrument.

account_id.description: Narrow to fees paid at ONE account (id from list_accounts). Omit to get every account AND the `by_account` per-venue rollup that lets you compare what each broker costs — filtering to one account collapses that comparison.

position_id.description: Which position (one instrument at one account) this lot lands on — position_id from get_portfolio. An unknown id is refused. If the account does not hold this instrument yet, use add_positions instead.

quantity.description: Number of UNITS acquired (shares/coins), never the trade's cash value. Must be positive and finite — zero or negative is refused rather than booking an empty lot.

unit_cost.description: Cost per unit in cost_currency, EXCLUDING fees — `fees` amortizes on top (effective basis/unit = unit_cost + fees/quantity). Omit ONLY when the basis is genuinely unknown: it stores as null (0 does too), and every later sale of this lot then reports realized_gain=null rather than a fabricated 0.

cost_currency.description: ISO 4217 code unit_cost and fees are quoted in (e.g. USD). Omitted: falls back to the position's cost_currency, then the portfolio base currency.

fees.description: TOTAL acquisition commission for this lot in cost_currency (not per unit), amortized into cost basis. Copy it off the broker confirmation; omit when the source shows none — don't estimate. Default 0.

funding_account_id.description: Cash account to debit for qty × unit_cost + fees, booked WITH the lot (ticker, quantity, memo). Omit only when that debit is already in the ledger. Unknown unit_cost skips the debit.

acquired_at.description: Acquisition date, ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Drives FIFO order (oldest sells first) and the holding-period clock classifying a later sale long- vs short-term. Omitted = undated: term reports 'unknown' and the double-book guard cannot fire.

kind.description: buy (default) | drp (dividend reinvestment) | transfer_in | grant | opening. An unrecognized value is silently stored as buy. The double-book guard covers buy/drp only — grant lots dedupe per tranche, so identical same-day vests are allowed.

idempotency_key.description: Per-item dedupe key — never one key for the whole batch (see the tool description).

allow_duplicate.description: true ONLY for genuinely separate identical fills — otherwise a FULLY-OPEN lot on this position with the same kind, acquired_at, quantity and unit_cost is REFUSED as a double-book (returns existing_lot_id). A partially-sold match counts as a real earlier fill, not a duplicate.

acquisitions.description: Batch form: record MULTIPLE buys/transfers-in/grants in ONE call (e.g. every trade in an imported broker statement). Every item needs its OWN idempotency_key, and the double-book guard applies PER ITEM — one already-booked trade is refused alone while the rest still record. One call covers them all, and raises ONE confirm card for the whole batch.

reason.description: Why this lot should be removed

lot_id.description: The lot to remove — lot id from get_lots. Must be FULLY OPEN: a lot any disposal has already consumed part of is refused (close it with dispose_lots instead). Deleting a lot erases its cost basis, so the parent position's quantity and basis are resynced from the lots that remain.

deletions.description: Batch form: delete SEVERAL orphaned/duplicate lots in ONE call. Each is deleted independently (a partially-consumed lot is refused for that item only). One call covers them all, and raises ONE confirm card for the whole batch.

position_id.description: Which position (one instrument at one account) is being sold down — position_id from get_portfolio. The same instrument at two custodians is two disposals.

quantity.description: Number of UNITS disposed (shares/coins), never the cash received. Selling more than the position's open lots hold is refused before any write.

proceeds_per_unit.description: GROSS sale price per unit in proceeds_currency, BEFORE disposal_fees. A taxable sale whose NET (this − disposal_fees/quantity) is not positive is REFUSED: booking a $0 sale would record the whole cost basis as a fabricated loss. To write off or gift a holding for no value use is_taxable=false.

proceeds_currency.description: ISO 4217 code the proceeds and fees are quoted in. Omitted: falls back to the position's cost_currency, then the base currency. Each consumed lot's basis is FX-converted into THIS currency before subtracting — currencies are never mixed.

disposal_fees.description: TOTAL selling commission for this disposal in proceeds_currency (not per unit). Reduces the realized gain and any cash deposited. Copy it off the confirmation; omit when the source shows none.

disposed_at.description: Sale date, ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to TODAY — pass the real trade date for a backdated sale, since this ends the holding-period clock and so decides each consumed lot's long- vs short-term classification.

method.description: 'fifo' (default) consumes oldest lots first, ordered by acquired_at then created_at. 'specific_id' consumes exactly the lots in lot_selection and REQUIRES it. Any other value is refused. The choice changes which basis is used, so it changes both the realized gain and the long/short split.

lot_id.description: Which lot to sell from — lot id from get_lots on this same position. An id that is not an open lot of this position is refused.

qty.description: Units to take from THIS lot (not the whole sale). Across the selection these must sum to the disposal's `quantity` — any under- or over-fill is refused rather than silently adjusted.

lot_selection.description: [{lot_id, qty}] naming exactly which lots to consume — REQUIRED when method is 'specific_id', ignored under fifo. Call get_lots for the ids. The qty values must sum to `quantity` or the disposal is refused.

is_taxable.description: true (default) books a realized gain/loss. false marks a transfer-out or gift: carries the cost basis out and realizes NOTHING (realized_gain is null, not 0), and is the only accepted way to record a disposal with no proceeds.

proceeds_account_id.description: Cash account to deposit the NET proceeds into (quantity × proceeds_per_unit − disposal_fees) — account id from list_accounts, normally the custodian's cash wallet. Booked as a transfer dated disposed_at, FX-converted to that account's currency. OMITTING IT BOOKS NO CASH: the lot and cash ledgers are separate, so the sale then removes the units with nothing credited back.

transfer_to_account_id.description: For shares MOVED to another of the user's own accounts (e.g. a workplace custodian → IBKR): the destination account id or exact name from list_accounts. Requires is_taxable=false, proceeds_per_unit=0 and no proceeds_account_id — a transfer moves shares, not money. Activity then shows ONE 'Transfer · <qty> units → <account>' row instead of an anonymous transfer-out. This records WHERE the shares went; it does NOT create the receiving lots — acquire them on the destination position with kind=transfer_in (same unit_cost and acquired_at as the consumed lots, so basis and holding period carry over). Omit for a gift or write-off.

idempotency_key.description: Dedupe key (broker order id, or email id + symbol + date). A second call with the same key is a no-op returning the existing event_id — automated flows MUST pass one so a reprocessed email or retry can never book the same sale twice.

disposals.description: Batch form: one call for several disposals, each applied (and double-book-guarded) independently. One call covers them all, and raises ONE confirm card for the whole batch.

event_id.description: realized-event id from get_realized_pnl. Required unless `event_ids` is used instead.

event_ids.description: Batch form: undo SEVERAL disposals in ONE call (e.g. reverting an entire botched import batch) — a list of event_ids. Each is undone independently; an event whose consumed lots no longer exist is refused for that item only. One call covers them all, and raises ONE confirm card for the whole batch. Omit the single `event_id` field when using this.

queries.description: Batch form: resolve MULTIPLE tickers/coins in ONE call instead of one call per symbol (e.g. every holding in a freshly-imported portfolio). Each item is either a bare ticker string (uses no overrides) or an object with its own asset_class/price_source/price_source_id/unit/allow_duplicate_symbol. Every item resolves INDEPENDENTLY — a per-symbol refusal (e.g. an ambiguous duplicate ticker REFUSED without allow_duplicate_symbol) is reported for THAT item only in `results`; every other item still resolves. Omit the single `query` field when using this.

dividend_rate_annual.description: Expected annual dividend as a CASH AMOUNT PER UNIT in the instrument's quote currency (2.40 = $2.40/share/year), NOT a yield or a percent. Drives the income forecast and dividend calendar. Setting it here protects it from a live price refresh — the fetched figure will never overwrite it once you've set it explicitly.

subtype.description: Decides how the mark is DERIVED: ssb = always par (100); tbill = zero-coupon, accretes issue_price→100 over issue→maturity; fd = 100 plus simple interest accrued to date; market and etf are quoted instead (manual clean price / Yahoo). Wrong subtype means a wrong holding value.

face_value.description: Par per HOLDING UNIT, default 100. A market bond uses 1000 with quantity = number of bonds; ssb/tbill/fd use 1 with quantity = principal. Multiplies every coupon (rate × face × quantity), so a wrong value scales income wrongly.

coupon_rate_annual.description: Annual coupon as a FRACTION, not a percent: 0.035 means 3.5%.

coupon_freq_months.description: Months between coupons (6 = semi-annual, 12 = annual). Omitted: no coupon schedule or calendar rows. Annual income is face x rate regardless.

issue_date.description: Issue date, ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Start of a tbill's accretion / fd's interest.

maturity_date.description: Maturity date, ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Anchors the coupon dates walking back from it, and ends a tbill's accretion. Omitted on a tbill: it holds flat at issue_price.

issue_price.description: Price paid at issue as a PERCENT OF PAR (98.5 = 98.5% of par), default 100 — not a currency amount. Drives the tbill discount that accretes to par.

bond_terms.description: Fixed-income terms — set asset_class='bond' first or they are DROPPED. A bond's mark is derived from these: valuation inputs, not labels.

quote_currency.description: The currency the instrument is PRICED in (3-letter ISO). Refused once price history exists — stored points are denominated in the old currency, so relabelling would re-denominate every historical valuation; re-bind price_source/price_source_id to a series in the right currency instead. On a yahoo/coingecko instrument the feed's answer wins.

price_source.description: Price feed: 'yahoo' | 'coingecko' (quoted USD) | 'manual' (manual_price is the mark). Changing it or price_source_id re-binds pricing identity: the old price series is dropped (when no other instrument reads it) and the new key's is fetched; a collision on the new key, or a yahoo id the feed won't price, is REFUSED.

price_source_id.description: The feed entry's id (yahoo symbol like 'KSTL.DE', coingecko id like 'bitcoin'). A yahoo re-bind must be CONFIRMED by a live fetch — an id yahoo won't price is refused.

manual_price.description: Price per unit in quote_currency for a manual instrument — the only thing that values it. Required to switch a feed-priced instrument to price_source='manual' (a pin); the feed's history is kept, so re-binding back finds it again. Never put a price in price_source_id.

symbol.description: Display ticker. Metadata — pricing identity is (price_source, price_source_id), not the symbol.

unit.description: Holding unit for physical metal (g|kg|ozt|tael|luong|tola|baht). Recomputes quote_per_unit; '' clears back to native shares/coins.

updates.description: Batch form: edit MULTIPLE instruments in ONE call (e.g. reclassifying several ETFs after enrichment). Each item names its own instrument_id plus the fields to change and is applied INDEPENDENTLY, so one unknown id doesn't block the rest — check each item's own result in `results`. Only the fields you pass change; a null is ignored, so a value cannot be cleared this way.

position_id.description: Which position to edit — position_id from get_portfolio.

changes.description: Fields to change: account_id, account_name. Any other key is REFUSED. quantity, cost_basis and cost_currency are NEVER editable — they are derived from the position's records (its lots; for a grant, its vesting schedule and vests), so record what happened instead with acquire_lots / dispose_lots, correct a wrong lot with update_lots, or use the grant tools. vesting_state is set only by the grant tools.

updates.description: Batch form: [{position_id, changes}, …] — one call for several positions. One call covers them all, and raises ONE confirm card for the whole batch. Omit position_id/changes when using this.

instrument_id.description: What is held — instrument_id from resolve_instruments (call it first for a ticker) or get_portfolio. An unknown id is refused rather than minting an instrument.

account_id.description: Where it is held — account id from list_accounts. Use the custodian's SECURITIES account, never its cash wallet: positions and lots live on the securities account.

account_name.description: Alternative to account_id: an existing securities account's exact name or institution (several matches are REFUSED, naming each), else CREATES a securities account of this name (e.g. 'IBKR'). Prefer account_id — a typo here creates a second account.

account_type.description: Type used ONLY when account_name has to CREATE the account; ignored otherwise. Almost always 'investment' (a brokerage or crypto exchange — holdings plus settlement cash), which is the default. 'retirement' for a CPF/SRS/401k that holds funds. The other five hold no market positions. The new account's currency comes from the instrument's quote currency.

quantity.description: Units held (shares/coins), not the position's cash value. For a bond priced off bond_terms with face_value 1 (ssb/tbill/fd) this is the principal.

cost_basis.description: AVERAGE COST PER UNIT in cost_currency (defaults to the instrument's quote currency) — NOT the total amount paid. Divide the total by quantity before passing it. 0 or omitted stores as unknown, which makes unrealized P&L and any later realized gain report null rather than a wrong number.

cost_currency.description: Original currency of the supplied per-unit cost basis. Preserve it even when the instrument is quoted in another currency; never convert historical cost at today's FX rate. Omit only when the cost is already in the quote currency.

vesting_state.description: 'vested' (default — the holding is the user's). 'unvested' is REFUSED here: unvested units come from an equity grant's vesting schedule, so create the grant instead. This is ENTITLEMENT, not liquidity — property is illiquid but perfectly vested. A second VESTED position for the same instrument at the same account is REFUSED with the existing position_id — a further buy of a holding already tracked is an acquire_lots call, not another position.

acquired_at.description: Acquisition date, ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Supplying it also records a real buy LOT for this quantity and cost (and any idempotency_key lands on that lot, so a later acquire_lots for the same trade dedupes instead of double-booking). ONLY a date the user actually gave — never a guess or a placeholder (not an account-opening date, not today, not an estimate the user didn't state). Unknown → OMIT it: the holding is then recorded as an OPENING BALANCE lot dated today (held when tracking started), which is the honest record; when the user later knows the real purchase date, set it on that lot with update_lots.

fees.description: Acquisition commission in cost_currency, amortized into the auto-created lot's basis.

idempotency_key.description: Per-item dedupe key (e.g. the broker order id) — never one key for the whole batch.

adds.description: Batch form: add MULTIPLE new holdings in ONE call (e.g. every position in a freshly-imported portfolio). Every item needs its OWN idempotency_key. One call covers them all, and raises ONE confirm card for the whole batch. Each is applied independently, so an instrument×account already holding an active position is refused alone (buy more via acquire_lots) while the rest still add.

position_id.description: position_id from get_portfolio. Required unless `removals` (the batch form) is used instead.

removals.description: Batch form: remove SEVERAL positions in ONE call — a list of position_ids. Each is removed independently; an unknown id is reported for that item only. Always has 'kind'. manual: {kind:'manual'}. schedule: {kind:'schedule', type:…} where type is once {at: ISO-8601 datetime}, daily|weekdays {time:'HH:MM', tzid?}, weekly {time, day:'mon'..'sun', tzid?}, monthly {time, day:1-31, tzid?}, interval {seconds:>=60}, or rrule {rrule: iCalendar RRULE body with FREQ and no 'RRULE:' prefix, dtstart?, tzid?} for anything the fixed types cannot express. event: {kind:'event', event:'txn'|'balance'|'price', when:{…}, limit:'each'|'hour'|'day'}. txn when: {conditions:[{field, op, value}]} — ALL must hold; omit for every transaction. account is|is_not <account id or name> (either side of a transfer); kind is|is_not expense|income|transfer|investment|investment_buy|investment_sale|adjustment (a buy pays out of the account, a sale pays in; investment = both); payee is|is_not <payee id or name> — these three take a list too (is = any of, is_not = none of); amount over|under <number> — absolute, in the account's currency when 'account is' names one account, else the base currency; description|memo contains|not_contains <comma-separated phrases, any counts>, starts_with|regex <text>. balance when: {account:<account id>, direction:'below'|'above', amount:<number in that account's currency>}. price when: {symbol:<any market ticker, e.g. 'AAPL', 'D05.SI'>, direction:'below'|'above' (a price in the ticker's own quote currency) or 'rise'|'fall'|'move' (% vs. the previous close), value:<number>}.

name.description: Short user-facing name for the Automation.

instructions.description: Exactly what the Automation should do when it runs — never WHEN: no schedule, cadence or trigger condition ('every Monday', 'when a charge over 500 posts'). The trigger is the only 'when', and each run is told its trigger and last completed run: say 'since the last run'.

description.description: Optional one-sentence explanation shown in the Automation list.

permission_mode.description: How much this Automation asks before acting: manual asks every time, auto proceeds except on hardline operations, skip proceeds regardless. Omit unless the user explicitly requested one.

status.description: Initial lifecycle state. Omit for active.

automation.description: Draft to validate without saving it.

tasks.description: The tasks to add, in the order you intend to do them.

subject.description: What this task accomplishes, in the words you would use telling the owner — "Read today's mail", not "email_search_messages". One short line.

description.description: Optional detail: what exactly this step covers, if the subject leaves it open.

task_id.description: The id returned when the task was added, e.g. "2".

dismissals.description: Dismiss several at once, same shape as above.

kind.description: Only this kind: 'file' (documents the user added or kept), 'artifact' (things you made that the user saved), 'statement' (imported bank statements), 'receipt' (transaction receipts), or 'asset' (files attached to an owned asset — `asset_name` says which).

year.description: Only items for this year, e.g. 2025.

tag.description: Only items the user gave this tag (case-insensitive), e.g. 'Apartment'.

query.description: Case-insensitive text matched against title, file name, note and tags.

limit.description: Items per page (default 20, max 50).

offset.description: Items to skip, for paging.

document_ids.description: Document ids (the `id` from list_documents, e.g. 'file-att_…'), up to 5 per call.

offset.description: Character offset into each file's text — pass a result's `next_offset` (with that one id) to continue a long document.

artifact_id.description: An artifact you made (create_artifact's id) to keep in Documents.

attachment_id.description: A file the user sent in chat (its attachment id) to keep in Documents. Keeping it again only updates the details below.

title.description: Files only: a clearer name than the file name.

year.description: Files only: the year it is for, e.g. 2025.

private.description: Files only: true marks it Private (you can no longer read it). You can never switch Private off — only the user can, in Documents.

transaction_ids.description: The flagged transactions to approve — get_transactions needs_review=true lists them. Only rows where needs_review is true are changed.

id.description: The Documents item's id, from list_documents (e.g. artifact-art_…).

artifact_id.description: Or an artifact you made (create_artifact's id), when you know that id.

reason.description: Why the lot is being corrected

lot_id.description: The lot to correct — lot id from get_lots.

acquired_at.description: The real purchase date the user gave, ISO YYYY-MM-DD (not in the future) — never a guess. The usual fix for an 'opening' lot dated the day the holding was added because no date was known.

quantity.description: Units in this lot (positive). The position's quantity follows its lots.

unit_cost.description: Cost PER UNIT in cost_currency — not the total paid.

fees.description: Acquisition fees in cost_currency, spread across the lot's units.

kind.description: buy | drp | transfer_in | opening. 'opening' = held when tracking started (counts at market value in returns); 'buy' = a purchase at its cost.

updates.description: Corrections, one per lot: [{lot_id, …fields to change}]. One call covers them all, and raises ONE confirm card for the whole batch.

tickers.description: Only these tickers, e.g. ['AAPL']. Omit for every thesis.

updates.description: One entry per ticker. Fields you omit keep their current value; `clear` blanks fields. Prices are in the instrument's quote currency.

ticker.description: The ticker whose thesis to write, e.g. 'AAPL'.

role.description: core = long-term base of the portfolio; satellite = an active bet around it; speculative = a small, high-risk bet.

reason.description: Why they own it, or would buy it, and how long they plan to hold if they said, e.g. 'holding to 2029'. At most 280 characters.

breaks_if.description: The business fact that would break the thesis and make them sell. At most 280 characters.

buy_above.description: Optional floor of the buy zone (needs buy_below).

trim_above.description: Price to trim or sell at.

query.description: A few words, e.g. 'house deposit' or a name; "double quotes" keep a phrase whole.

limit.description: Max conversations to return (default 5, max 10).

session_id.description: The conversation's id, as search_past_conversations returns it.

offset.description: Messages to skip from the start.

limit.description: Max messages to return (default 20, max 50).

handles.description: The handles of the Recent entries this run has done what they said, as shown beside each entry in your memory block (e.g. 'm7a88f8').
